properties.name: Old Mill Creek
properties.story: Ran past the tide mill that named it, into the head of Jamaica Bay.

properties.name: Spring Creek
properties.story: Marsh creek on the Brooklyn-Queens line, filled behind the Belt Parkway.

properties.name: Sunfish Pond
properties.story: A pond at Park Avenue and 32nd, drained when Madison Avenue was cut through.

properties.name: Turtle Bay creek
properties.story: Ran down to the cove at East 47th that gave Turtle Bay its name.

properties.name: Coney Island Creek
properties.story: Once cut Coney Island off from Brooklyn; the eastern half was filled in the 1930s and 60s.

properties.name: Alley Creek
properties.story: The Alley’s tidal creek and mill pond at the head of Little Neck Bay.

properties.name: Paerdegat Basin
properties.story: The old Paerdegat creek and its marsh, cut back to a single dredged basin.

properties.name: Horse Brook
properties.story: Crossed Elmhurst to the Flushing meadows; gone under the Long Island Expressway.

properties.name: Wallabout Creek
properties.story: The creek and mill pond at Wallabout Bay, filled for the Navy Yard.

properties.name: English Kills
properties.story: The far branch of Newtown Creek, reaching into Bushwick; most of it is now built over.

properties.name: Fresh Creek
properties.story: Drained the Flatlands marsh into Jamaica Bay; the upper creek is under Starrett City.

properties.name: Maspeth Creek
properties.story: A north branch of Newtown Creek through the Maspeth meadows.

properties.name: Dutch Kills
properties.story: The Long Island City branch of Newtown Creek, shortened and bulkheaded.

properties.name: Minetta Brook
properties.story: Passed the west side of Washington Square; Minetta Lane and Minetta Street still trace it.

properties.name: Sunswick Creek
properties.story: Ran through Astoria to the East River; buried as a sewer line.

properties.name: Harlem Creek
properties.story: Montayne’s Rivulet drained the Harlem flats east to the Harlem River.

properties.name: Minetta Brook
properties.story: Turned west below Downing Street and reached the Hudson near Charlton.

properties.name: Great Kill
properties.story: Drained the west thirties and forties and met the Hudson around West 42nd.

properties.name: Canal Street canal
properties.story: The ditch cut to drain the Collect Pond to the Hudson; Canal Street is built on it.

properties.name: Manhattanville stream
properties.story: Ran down the Manhattanville hollow, the valley West 125th Street still follows.

properties.name: Springfield Creek
properties.story: Fed from Baisley Pond down to Jamaica Bay through the Springfield meadows.

properties.name: Flushing Creek
properties.story: Its tidal meadows became the ash dump, then the 1939 World’s Fair grounds.

properties.name: Canal Street canal
properties.story: The ditch cut to drain the Collect Pond to the Hudson; Canal Street is built on it.

properties.name: Collect Pond
properties.story: The city’s drinking water until it was fouled and filled in 1811.

properties.name: Harlem Creek
properties.story: Its headwater marsh survives as the Harlem Meer.
